Fix the source split $a(S)=v_{and}(x_S),o(S)=v_{or}(x_S)$ with $a+o=g$, $a(\varnothing)=b,o(\varnothing)=0$. Möbius inversion gives $a(S)=\sum_{T\subseteq S}I_a(T)=b+\sum_{\varnothing\ne T\subseteq S}I_a(T)$, counting the empty term once.

Put $h(L)=o(N\setminus L)$. Nonempty OR coefficients are $O(T)=-I_h(T)$. Their full sum is $h(\varnothing)-h(N)=o(N)-o(\varnothing)$, while the sum inactive on $S$ is $h(\varnothing)-h(N\setminus S)=o(N)-o(S)$. Subtract to obtain $o(S)-o(\varnothing)=o(S)$ and add the AND component. The second OR grouping in F.1 does not correctly exclude disjoint activations; the full-minus-inactive proof repairs the same theorem.

Main Eq.(2) explicitly defines component dividends only for nonempty S, whereas Eq.(3) sums over all T⊆N, including an unspecified empty AND coefficient. This is first a domain/convention gap. Under the ordinary Möbius extension, the empty AND coefficient is a(empty)=b. The constant network v=1 with a=1,o=0 has empty coefficient one and zero nonempty coefficients, so this extension of Eq.(3) gives two rather than one. Setting the empty AND coefficient to zero avoids duplication but is not specified in Eq.(2). Eq.(4) uses only nonempty AND terms and avoids this extension. The residual of salient truncation in Eq.(5) is the two omitted activated sums and is bounded by their absolute tails; no uniform small-tail premise is supplied.

The source imposes no analyticity restriction on the DNN or input and uses a global Taylor equality. Take the one-variable ReLU network $v(t)=\max(t-1/2,0)$, baseline $r=0$, and $x=1$. The network vanishes near the baseline, so all derivatives at $0$ vanish. Its Taylor right side is zero whereas $I(\{1\})=v(1)-v(0)=1/2$. This refutes the unrestricted statement; adding analyticity would change it.

A separate valid finite-polynomial result remains: a monomial of support $A$ obeys $m_A(z^S)=\mathbf1_{A\subseteq S}m_A(z)$ because masked positive-degree coordinates annihilate it. Grouping by support reconstructs every mask, and uniqueness identifies those coefficients with actual dividends. This does not prove the unrestricted Taylor claim.

The cancellation in Eq.(27) requires both $w_T\ne0$ and a valid Taylor expansion. A constant network is allowed and has every nonempty $w_T=0$, making the printed $J_T$ contain $0/0$. This is a domain issue, and a binary value cannot be silently assigned to zero coefficients.

Where the printed expression is defined, write its numerator as $K_T$. The support mask identity gives $K_T(\hat x_S)=\mathbf1_{T\subseteq S}K_T(\hat x)$ and $K_T(\hat x)=w_T$. Nonzero normalization yields $J_T(\hat x_S)=\mathbf1_{T\subseteq S}$. Consequently $f(\hat x_S)=\sum_{T\subseteq S}w_T=v(\hat x_S)$, with $w_\varnothing=b,J_\varnothing=1$. An independently defined binary model does not repair the zero denominator in the source Taylor definition.

Linearity gives $\Delta I_T=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}\Delta v_L$ without independence. Finite expectation linearity gives zero mean from the marginal laws.

The main statement specifies only Gaussian marginals $\Delta v_L\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$.  For one variable use the same $Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$ for both masks, $\Delta v_\varnothing=\Delta v_{\{1\}}=Z$. All stated marginal conditions hold, but $\Delta I_{\{1\}}=Z-Z=0$ has variance zero rather than $2\sigma^2$ when $\sigma>0$. F.3 adds iid noise to eliminate covariance.

The separate independent model has a real probability proof: every sign has square $1$, so the variance is $\sum_{L\subseteq T}\sigma^2=2^{|T|}\sigma^2$. For $w_T\ne0$, scaling gives trigger variance $2^{|T|}\sigma^2/w_T^2$; its proportionality factor depends on $T$. Assumption 1 introduces another model and does not follow automatically.

The sum of expectations depends only on the common row marginals, without requiring cross-row independence; one random family represents those marginals, rather than imposing perfect row correlation on the source. The original uniform average is explicitly meanNoisyLoss, whose positive cardinality normalization preserves the unique minimizer.
